# Converting metric units for area and volume
## Key points
* Area and volume are usually measured in metric units. An area can be measured in centimetres squared (cm²) or metres squared (m²). Volume is often measured in centimetres cubed (cm³) or metres cubed (m³).
* When comparing or combining an area or volume it is important to measure the objects using the same units. Without converting the areas into the same unit, it might be difficult to tell, for example, whether 400cm² is bigger (or smaller) than 4m².
* A common misconception could be when someone thinks that the conversion between two different lengths would be the same conversion between two different areas. For example, 1 m is the same as 100 cm but 1 m² is not the same as 100 cm².

...

## Converting units for area
* Objects can be measured in different units, depending on their size. It is important to know the conversions between metric units.
* The method for converting between units for area works in a similar way to converting between units of length. However, it is important to remember that an area has two dimensions .
* When you are converting one type of unit to another you need to know how many smaller units are needed to make one larger unit.

...

### Examples
1. Example one. An image of a square. The length and width of the square are labelled as one metre. Written above: one metre squared equals question mark centimetres squared. The question mark is coloured orange.
Image caption,
Work out how many centimetres squared (cm²) would be needed to cover an area of 1 metre squared (1 m²)
2. The same image of the labelled square. Written above: one metre equals one hundred centimetres.
One metre squared does not equal one hundred centimetres squared.
Image caption,
A common misconception would be that 100 cm² are needed because 1 metre is 100 centimetres. This is incorrect.
3. A series of two images. The first image is the same labelled square as the previous. The second image is the same square. The length and width of the square have been relabelled as one hundred centimetres.
Image caption,
When converting between units for an area calculation, remember that a square has two dimensions, the length and the width. Draw two identical squares next to one another. Label one in metres (1 m by 1 m). 1 metre is equivalent to 100 centimetres. Label the other square in centimetres (100 cm by 100 cm).
4. The same images as the previous. Written beneath the first square: one metre multiplied by one metre equals one metre squared.

...

One metre multiplied by one metre equals one metre squared. One hundred centimetres multiplied by one hundred centimetres equals ten thousand centimetres squared. One metre squared equals ten thousand centimetres squared. Written below: Five metre squared equals fifty thousand centimetres squared. Written beneath: Thirty thousand centimetres squared equals three metres squared.
Image caption,
When converting between units for an area calculation convert both dimensions (the length and width) to the required unit before finding the area. Use these to calculate the area conversion factor. When converting from a larger unit to a smaller unit (eg m² to cm²) you multiply. When converting from a smaller unit to a larger unit (eg mm² to cm²) you divide.
7. Example two. Sixty thousand centimetres squared equals question mark metres squared.
The question mark is coloured orange.
Image caption,
Convert 60,000 cm² into m². 1 m = 100 cm. 1 m² = 100 cm x 100 cm = 10, 000 cm². Conversion factor is 10,000
8. One metre squared equals ten thousand centimetres squared. Written below: Sixty thousand centimetres squared equals sixty thousand divided by ten thousand equals six metres squared. The six metres squared is coloured orange.
Image caption,
The smaller unit (cm²) is converted to a larger unit (m²).
To do this, divide 60,000 cm² = 60,000 ÷ 10,000 = 6 m².
9. Example three. Twenty centimetres squared equals question mark millimetres squared. The question mark is coloured orange.
Image caption,
Convert 20 cm² into mm². 1 cm = 10 mm. 1 cm² = 10 mm x 10 mm = 100 mm². Conversion factor is 100
10. One centimetre squared equals one hundred millimetres squared. Written below: Twenty centimetres squared equals twenty multiplied by one hundred equals two thousand millimetres squared.
The two thousand millimetres squared is coloured orange.
Image caption,
The larger unit (m²) is converted to a smaller unit (cm²). To do this, multiply 20 cm² = 20 × 100 = 2,000 mm².

## Converting units for volume
* Objects can be measured in different units, depending on their size. It is important to know the conversions between metric units.
* The method for converting between units for volume works in a similar way to converting between units of length, however it is important to remember that a volume has three dimensions .
* When you are converting one type of unit to another you need to know how many smaller units are needed to make 1 larger unit.

...

### Examples
1. Example one. An image of a cube. The length, width and height of the cube are labelled as one metre. Written above: one metre cubed equals question mark centimetres cubed. The question mark is coloured orange.
Image caption,
Work out how many centimetres cubes would be needed to equal a volume of 1 metre cubed.
2. The same image of the cube as the previous.
Image caption,
A common misconception would be that there would be 100 because 1 metre is 100 centimetres.

...

Label one in metres (1 m by 1 m by 1 m). 1 metre is equivalent to 100 centimetres. Label the other cube in centimetres (100 cm by 100 cm by 100 cm).
4. The same images as the previous. Written beneath the first cube: one metre multiplied by one metre multiplied by one metre equals one metre cubed. Written beneath the second cube: one hundred centimetres multiplied by one hundred centimetres multiplied by one hundred centimetres equals one million centimetres cubed.
Image caption,
The volume of the cube labelled in metres is 1 m x 1 m x 1 m = 1 m³. The volume of the cube labelled in centimetres is 100 cm x 100 cm x 100 cm = 1,000,000 cm³.
5. One metre cubed equals one million centimetres cubed.
Image caption,
1,000,000 cubic centimetres would be needed to create the same volume as 1 metre cubed.
6. One metre multiplied by one metre multiplied by one metre equals one metre cubed.
Written below: One hundred centimetres multiplied by one hundred centimetres multiplied by one hundred centimetres equals one million centimetres cubed.
Image caption,
When converting between units for a volume calculation convert all three dimensions (the length, width and height) to the required unit before finding the volume. Use these to calculate the volume conversion factor. When converting from a larger unit to a smaller unit (eg m³ to cm³) you multiply.
When converting from a smaller unit to a larger unit (eg mm³ to cm³) you divide.
7. Example two. Fifty thousand millimetres cubed equals question mark centimetres cubed. The question mark is coloured orange.
Image caption,
Convert 50,000 mm³ into cm³. 1 cm = 10 mm. 1 cm³ = 10 mm x 10 mm x 10 mm = 1000 mm³. Conversion factor is 1000
8. One centimetre cubed equals one thousand millimetres cubed.

...

1 m³ = 100 cm x 100 cm x 100 cm = 1,000,000 cm³. Conversion factor is 1,000,000
10. One metre cubed equals one million centimetres cubed. Written below: Four metres cubed equals four multiplied by one million equals four million centimetres cubed. The four million centimetres is coloured orange.
Image caption,
The larger unit (m³) is converted to a smaller unit (m³). To do this, multiply 4m³ = 4 × 1,000,000 = 4,000,000 cm³.
